column3: Near-parallel auditory exclusion: adds that the protected setting excludes laghw alongside ta'thim, broadening the speech ethic without collapsing the two.
Its universal dhikr claim offers only a remote contrast to the local acoustic condition of 78:35.
Frames turning away from laghw as an active discipline of attention, not merely the absence of sound.
Near-parallel setting: laghw is not heard, while salam is explicitly retained, supporting ordered speech rather than silence.
A nearby reward item helps situate 78:35 within the described favorable environment but adds no speech distinction.
The recurring challenge about takdhib is a secondary contrast to 78:35's kizdhab, not an equivalent lexical claim.
Near-parallel auditory exclusion of laghiyah reinforces that the reward setting is cleared of degrading or empty speech.
